builds.detail: From Brett's attachment (Oct 27 2026): 5 deliverables — TS data contracts (layout & component tree, theme engine, plugin manifest), Pydantic v2 validator/migrator + ingestion namespacing, React error boundary + pub/sub lifecycle broker, project spec, developer docs (new plugin, harvesting, live sync). Built ON the existing contracts (asset@1, plugin@1, appearance@1), not beside them. Web + Python; Android twins deferred.

origin.said: 5 deliverables — TS data contracts (layout & component tree, theme engine, plugin manifest), Pydantic v2 validator/migrator + ingestion namespacing, React error boundary + pub/sub lifecycle broker, project spec, developer docs (new plugin, harvesting, live sync). Built ON the existing contracts (asset@1, plugin@1, appearance@1), not beside them. Web + Python; Android twins deferred.

steps.text: Gap audit: map attachment items 1-3 onto what exists (asset@1 layout, color/style themes, plugin@1, AxfWebLibrary, settings, embed); write _claude/memory/docs/arch-foundation.md listing only what is new. Do not duplicate existing contracts.
Layout & component tree contract (TS): page → widget/plugin nodes with unique ids, dimensions, bounding boxes, asset dependencies; additive to layout@ assets; fixture + checker.
Theme contract additions: component-specific overrides on top of color/style themes (tokens only); fixture.
plugin@1 manifest additions: declared assets, default settings, layout entry points (optional fields, old manifests still valid); schema + validators.

Pydantic v2 models mirroring items 1-3 + migration engine (@model_validator(mode="before")): up-cast legacy versions, fill missing fields, sanitise; never crash old apps. framework/python/axf/contracts/.
Ingestion namespace engine: prefix every harvested plugin key as plugin_id:property (state + assets), idempotent, collision report; same rules in TS + Python, one fixture.
Lifecycle event broker (TS): onInit / onStateChange / onThemeUpdate / onContextMenuOpen / onDestroy, typed message passing, plugins never touch global state; fixture.
React PluginBoundary: error boundary around every mounted plugin (layout + context-menu hooks), isolate the widget, themed fallback stub, report to rt.diagnostics.
Architecture spec: add the new contracts to CLAUDE.md status + a reference layout tree in framework/spec/ARCH-FOUNDATION.md (no second .claude.md: CLAUDE.md is the project file).
Developer guide part 1: build a new plugin (manifest, layout/theme hooks, lifecycle hooks) in apps/console-web/plugins/README.md.
Developer guide part 2: how harvesting works + how live sync works (hub appearance@1, migrations) in framework/spec/.
Tests in CI for the new checkers + Python test; THREADS.md + PORTING.md (Android twins deferred).

origin.said: Create 3 completely different looks, feels, behavior. Existing look now in a tab holding main window and 2 more tabs with entirely worked out GUIs that are essentially different apps as far as look is concerned. Make plugin for this app and every app to roll a new interface that rebuilds every single thing about user interface, menus, context menus, logos, etc.

steps.text: interface@1: one asset that names a whole interface: design package (style, colour, layout, behaviour), branding (logos, animated logos, icon pack), every chrome asset (banner, app menu, toolbar, nav, context menus, tab group, settings interface, dialog/window/container styles). Open slot list, so new chrome joins by itself.
Scoped runtime: the same app drawn under several interfaces at once (one asset scope + CSS scope per interface, nothing leaks between them). Engine part + fixture.
steps.why: runtime internals (theme scoping was never built)

steps.text: React layer: <InterfaceScope id> wraps a subtree; AppShell, menus, context menus, dialogs, floating windows and portals honour the scope.
steps.why: changes how GUIs work across apps

steps.text: Interface roller engine 1/2: seeded, coherent roll of every slot (palette harmony + contrast, type pairing, radii/density/elevation, motion, layout) with a lock per part; reproducible; fixture.

Roller 2/2: rolls structure too: app menu / toolbar / nav / context-menu arrangements built from the app's own actions (never drops one), plus a new logo, animated logo and icon pack through the brand generators.
Interface 2 part 1: an entirely different look, feel and behaviour (design package, branding, chrome assets).
Interface 2 part 2: menus, context menus, dialogs, windows and containers worked out and checked on every page.
Interface 3 part 1: a third, entirely different look, feel and behaviour.
Interface 3 part 2: menus, context menus, dialogs, windows and containers worked out and checked on every page.
The GizmoX console's main window becomes a tab group: Main (today's look, unchanged) · Interface 2 · Interface 3, each tab the full app under its own interface scope.
Interface roller console plugin 1/2: Roll, lock parts, roll again, preview in a new tab, undo.
Roller 2/2: save as an interface@1 asset, apply to one tab or the whole app, export / import, settings tab + lifecycle.
Harvest it as framework library lib-interface-roller so every AXF web app can install it (console, AmberX, axHub web, Patches web, Walkthrough Studio); library@1 parts.
Install the library in the AmberX app and the other web apps; check each one builds and rolls.
Tests for every checker, before/after shots of the three tabs, rebuild report, PORTING.md (Android deferred), CLAUDE.md, THREADS.md.

builds.title: Every UI element is a named asset
builds.detail:
Apply the rule across schemas/asset-types.json, the web and Android ports, the 39 starter assets and the conformance fixtures.

- Two tiers: element assets (button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label...) and parent assets (toolbar, menu, nav, app menu, dialog, container, window). A standalone element in a layout is its own named asset; groups only exist inside a parent asset.
- Namespaced ids for every asset (e.g. axf.button.save, axf.toolbar.editor); layouts and parents reference ids.
- Split instance (label, icon, action, state) from skin (style asset + theme tokens).
- Slots with type contracts in layout regions and parents; hot-swap and drag-and-drop = rebinding a slot to a compatible asset id.
- Kernel unchanged (open type registry).

notes.text: Overlaps settings-asset (new `settings` asset type, branch claude/project-thread-55oakl); build with settings-asset-fable.

steps.text: Design note first: write `_claude/memory/docs/named-assets.md` — the two tiers (element assets: button, slider, toggle, input, icon, label; parent assets: toolbar, menu, nav, app-menu, dialog, container, window), the id namespace rule (`<ns>.<type>.<name>`, e.g. `axf.button.save`), instance vs skin split, and which existing starter ids change. List every file the rule touches. No code.

BRETT: review the design note. Decide (a) whether existing starter ids are renamed in place or aliased (old id keeps resolving), (b) whether element assets are required for every control or opt-in per app. Record both answers in the note and in `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Schema: in `framework/schemas/asset-types.json` add `"tier": "element" | "parent"` to every type and a top-level `idRule` (regex, documented) for namespaced ids; keep `optional: true` on new fields so old apps validate. Run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs schemas` and `axf validate --framework` — both must pass unchanged.

Validator (web): `framework/core/validate.ts` → `validateAsset` warns (not errors, until the switch flips) when an id does not match `idRule`; add `assetTier(type)`. Add 4 cases to `framework/spec/fixtures/validation.json` (good namespaced id, bare id, element, parent). `npx -y tsx framework/spec/gen-fixtures.mts` then CI check.

Validator (Kotlin + CLI): mirror the id rule in `framework/android/axf-kernel/.../asset/` validator and in the build-engine validator (`framework/cli/build-engine.mjs` validateAsset). Same fixture cases replayed by `ConformanceTest` (written without a compiler: check the "CI build errors" issue after push).

Element asset types, part 1: add `toggle`, `input`, `icon` as `tier: element` types in `asset-types.json` (data shape: label, icon, action, state keys; skin = style-theme tokens only). One starter each under `framework/assets/<type>/`. `axf validate --framework` passes.

Element asset types, part 2: mark the existing `button`, `slider`, `label` as `tier: element`; add the instance/skin split to their spec (`data.instance` {label, icon, action, state} vs `data.skin` {style tokens}) with the old flat shape still accepted by `asEnvelope` normalisation. Fixture cases in `components.json`.

Parent slots: in `asset-types.json` give every parent type (toolbar, app-menu, nav-menu, context-menu, dialog, container, window) a `slots` block like `layout.slots` (named slots + accepted element types), reusing `compileSlots`/`regionAccepts` from `framework/core/engines/layout.ts`. Fixture cases in `layout-slots.json` for one parent.

Rebinding = hot-swap: `framework/core/runtime.ts` gets `bindSlot(parentType, parentId, slot, elementId)` / `unbindSlot` (stored like `attachToHost` in `widgets.ts`, settings key `axf.bind.<parent>.<slot>`); `swap()` of a parent keeps bindings whose types still fit. Unit cases in `widgets.json` → `bindings`.

Kotlin runtime parity: `AxfRuntime.bindSlot/unbindSlot` + KV `<key>:bind` in the kernel, same rules as the TS version, replaying the `bindings` fixture in `ConformanceTest`. Written without a compiler; push and read the CI issue.

Rename the 39 starter assets to namespaced ids (`axf.<type>.<name>`) with the alias map chosen in step 2 (`framework/assets/aliases.json`, read by `registry.ts` + Kotlin `AssetRegistry`): every app manifest and `framework/defaults.json` still resolve. `axf validate --framework` + `validate apps/demo` + console `npm run build` pass.

React layer: `framework/react/components/Controls.tsx` renders an element asset by id (`<AssetButton id>` etc.) reading instance + skin; a standalone element in a layout region renders through the same path. Element Explorer (`react/studio/Inspector.tsx`) shows tier + bindings.

Compose layer: `axf-ui/components/Buttons.kt`, `Slider.kt`, `Controls.kt` take an element asset id the same way; `ElementExplorer.kt` shows tier + bindings. Android console showcase renders one bound element in its toolbar.

Flip the switch: `idRule` violations become errors for apps with `frameworkVersion` ≥ the new one (old apps keep warnings), `axf init` writes namespaced ids, templates updated. Run the CI template sweep locally (`axf init` for react-ts, next-ts, android-compose + validate).

Docs + close: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Named assets"; CLAUDE.md Status bullet; decisions.md entry; mark the pending item complete and the plan feature built; differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/named-asset-rule.md` (rule for rebuilds).

builds.title: Asset Designer plugin (no-code)
builds.detail: No-code editors for nav menus, drawers, app menus, context menus, toolbars, layouts, style packs and color themes. Every asset validates against its schema before save. Adds a drawer asset type. Installed by default.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton: copy `apps/console-web/plugins/_template` to `plugins/asset-designer` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-designer`, `uiEditor: "builder"`, lifecycle block, `install.mjs`/`uninstall.mjs`), nav → Plugins → Asset designer, Settings → Plugins sub-tab (parent `plugins`). `node framework/cli/plugin-lifecycle.mjs check asset-designer` passes; console tsc + vite build pass.

Designer shell `web/Designer.tsx`: type picker (every non-attachable type from `asset-types.json` the designer covers: nav-menu, drawer, app-menu, context-menu, toolbar, layout, style-theme, color-theme), id + label fields, Save/Cancel; `useEditorSync()` so it reloads values on focus (UI-editor rule). Saves nothing yet.

Validation gate: every save runs `validateAsset` from the baked `src/axf/core/validate.ts`; errors shown inline next to the field they name; Save disabled until clean. Server route `POST /api/plugins/asset-designer/validate` mirrors it with the CLI validator (`framework/core/project-check.mjs` pattern). Test in `test.py`.

Storage: designed assets saved as asset@1 files under `.axf-console/plugins/asset-designer/assets/<type>/<id>.json` (lifecycle dataDir), served by `GET /api/plugins/asset-designer/assets`, registered into the runtime on load like the theme-manager plugin does (`registry.register`, origin `asset-designer`). Built-in ids refused.

Menu editor (nav-menu, app-menu, context-menu): tree of items (label, icon, action, children, divider), drag to reorder, action picker from `rt.actions.list()`, live preview via `rt.swap` on a `ad-preview-<type>` id. Reuses `MenuList.tsx` for the preview.

Toolbar editor: items (icon, label, action, badge counter), `density`/`surface`/`divider`/`collapsible`, widgets start/end picker from `attachable` types (engine-rpc `app-defaults` → `widgets`), live preview through the React `Toolbar`.

`drawer` asset type: add it to `asset-types.json` (hideable chrome, `side` left/right, `width`, `items` like nav-menu, `modal`), `layout.slots` accept it in the `drawer` region, starter `framework/assets/drawer/amberx-side.json`, `framework/defaults.json` names it. Validators on all three ports accept it (Kotlin: `AssetTypeSpec` resource); fixture case in `layout-slots.json`.

Drawer rendering: React `components/Chrome.tsx` draws the drawer region; Compose `axf-ui/components/Chrome.kt` the same (swipe from the edge, scrim from `--fx-opacity-scrim`). Drawer editor in the designer (same editor as nav-menu plus side/width/modal).

Layout editor: region grid (9 regions from `layout.slots`), per-region size/visibility, `data.slots` overrides with accepted-type chips; preview through `compileLayout`. Hidden slots greyed like Appearance does.

Color-theme editor: token groups from the theme engine (`core/engines/theme.ts` token list), colour pickers, contrast warnings (reuse `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks), light/dark pair, preview via `rt.swap`.
Style-theme editor: space, radii, borders, font sizes, opacity tokens (`opacityDisabled/Muted/Hover/Tint/Scrim/Glass`), density; preview; numbers clamped to the ranges known themes use.

Templates hook: "Start from" picker listing starters + designed assets + (later) `x.assets.templates` entries; Duplicate / Rename / Export JSON / Import JSON (validated). Export writes a file a user can drop into an app's assets folder.

Installed by default: plugin `enabled: true` in the console's plugin defaults, `framework/catalog/plugins.json` entry (planned → built resolves by itself), `node framework/cli/plugins.mjs --check`, status.json + tracker; Plugin Manager shows it.

Android face (first slice): `axf-devtools` gets an `AssetDesignerModule` placeholder route `asset-designer` listing designed assets received from the console (read-only), so the plugin-inventory shows it on both ports; full editors stay web-only for now (noted as a placeholder capability `axf.designer`).

Tests: plugin `test.py` (validate route, storage, built-in id refused, lifecycle), web unit cases for the drawer slot + layout compile, CI line; `uninstall.mjs --all` leaves nothing (`check --after-uninstall`).

Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-designer.md` (new plugin, so a build report), LOG.md line, web screenshots via `rebuild-shots.mjs`, CLAUDE.md Status, plan epic `x.assets.designer` built via `build_step`, pending item complete.

builds.title: Asset Browser plugin
builds.detail: Browse, preview, import, export and hot-swap assets across apps built on AXF. Installed by default.

steps.text: Plugin skeleton `apps/console-web/plugins/asset-browser` from `_template` (id `ai.amberx.axf.console.asset-browser`, lifecycle, install/uninstall, nav → Plugins → Asset browser, settings sub-tab). Lifecycle check + console build pass.

Sources: server route `GET /api/plugins/asset-browser/sources` lists asset folders it may read: framework starters (`framework/assets`), every app under `apps/*/src/assets` or `app/src/main/assets/axf` (from `framework/cli/app-bundle.mjs list`), designed assets (asset-designer dataDir when present). Never follows symlinks; roots only.
Browse view: grid by type → source → asset, search box (reuses `consoleSearch.ts` provider pattern), type chips from `asset-types.json`, counts per source. Rows show id, label, origin, tier.

Preview: `AssetPreview.tsx` from `framework/react/studio` renders the selected asset in a card; for chrome types a live preview on an `ab-preview-<type>` swap like theme-manager; "Apply here" = `rt.swap(type, id)` after `registry.register`.

Import: drop/paste JSON or pick a file → `validateAsset` → preview → install into a chosen target (console runtime, or an app folder through `POST /api/plugins/asset-browser/install {source, target, type, id}` that writes the file only inside allowed app asset folders; built-in ids refused; backups under the plugin dataDir).

Export: single asset or a pack (zip of asset@1 files + `pack.json`), served by `GET …/export?ids=`; packs are what the plugin runtime (`x.plugins`, PACK kind) will load later, so write the `pack@1` shape now in `framework/schemas/asset-pack.json`.

Hot-swap across apps: for apps running `axf dev` (`framework/cli/dev-server.mjs`), "Push to device" posts the asset to the dev server's folder so the HotReloader picks it up; list dev servers from settings (`axf.devServer`). Error card when none.

Installed by default + Android: enabled in console plugin defaults, `plugins.json` catalog entry, `plugins.mjs --check`; Android `axf-devtools` route `asset-browser` showing the bundled assets by type with Apply (uses `AssetRegistry` + `AxfRuntime.swap`), so Settings → Plugins lists it on both ports.
Tests: `test.py` (sources never leave roots, import validation, built-in refusal, export pack shape), lifecycle check, CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/asset-browser.md` + LOG.md + web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, plan `x.assets.browser` built, pending complete.

builds.title: Plugin manager + settings tabs for every app (Fable rebuild)
builds.detail: Every plugin gets a plugin-manager entry (info, enable/disable, view logs, settings). Plugins never ship their own settings screen; they add tabs to the app settings interface. Every app compiled by the build engine ships the settings interface and lib-settings. The Opus version is the console plugin `plugin-manager` (web console only: four views cards/table/detail/dependency graph in four layouts Studio/Mission control/Terminal/Catalog, default context-menu link, dependencies in detail, opens each plugin's UI and settings, logs, files, install & uninstall). Remove it first with its uninstall script (uninstall.mjs --all --publish), then build the cross-port version following plugin-lifecycle@1 (Android kernel + every app the build engine compiles), keeping the UI-editor rules (last save wins per key; reload current values on open/load/focus).

steps.text: Template index: `framework/assets/templates/index.json` (`asset-templates@1`: id, type, label, tags, file) + loader `listAssetTemplates(type)` in `framework/cli/build-engine.mjs`; engine-rpc `asset-templates`, console `GET /api/asset-templates?type=`. Empty list works end to end.

Validation in CI: `framework/spec/check-asset-templates.mjs` loads every template, runs `validateAsset`, checks unique ids, ≥ 10 per covered type once a type is marked `complete` in the index, and that each type has a `default`. Wire into `android.yml` (node job).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

nav-menu ×10: side nav, bottom tabs, rail, grouped sections, icon-only, with badges, two-level, settings-first, admin, minimal. Each a valid `nav-menu` asset in `framework/assets/templates/nav-menu/`.
app-menu ×10 (file/edit/view style menus, single-page apps, tool apps…) + context-menu ×10 (text, list row, card, media, dev, file, link, minimal, with submenus, keyboard hints).
toolbar ×10: editor, media, search-first, compact icons, labelled, split start/end with widgets, status-heavy (counters/progress), collapsible, roomy, minimal.
layout ×10: dashboard, master-detail, sidebar-left/right, bottom-nav phone, kiosk, editor + inspector, chat, settings, full-bleed, three-pane. Each with `data.slots` where it narrows a region.
drawer ×10 (needs `asset-designer` step 7's `drawer` type): left/right, modal/non-modal, wide/narrow, with header, grouped, icon rail, account-first, admin, minimal.

color-theme ×10 light + ×10 dark (pairs): contrast-checked with `theme-manager/web/rollEngine.ts` checks run from a script; names in one family (`arctic-daylight` style). Each pair shares a `pair` tag.
style-theme ×10: glass, flat, outlined, dense, roomy, rounded, square, hairline, soft, print. Numbers inside ranges known themes use; every opacity token present.

Defaults: `framework/defaults.json` + `framework/app-defaults.json` reviewed so every type has a default template id (new field `templates.default.<type>` read by `axf init` for "start from a template"); `axf init --template-set <id>` option registered in `build-options.json` only if it sets a token, else as an init argument.

Run once; commit shots ≤ 60 KB each (`framework/cli/shrink-shots.py`).

Android: templates bundled into `axf-assets` as a resource folder so Compose previews (`ComponentGallery.kt`) and the future Android designer read the same files; `AssetTemplates` Kotlin loader + a unit test that every bundled template validates.

builds.title: Port engine: bring a non-AXF app onto AmberX AXF (bake or rebuild)
builds.detail:
Runs the ports that claude-project parks (pending items port-<name>, manifest x.port, plan in the project at _claude/memory/docs/port-to-axf.md). Brett chose: ask each time between the two ways.

- bake: keep the codebase, run axf init into it (react-ts / next-ts / android-compose), then move its look and chrome into asset@1 assets step by step (colour/style themes, menus, toolbars, nav, dialogs, layout with region slots); UI reads engine tokens only (THEMING.md). Old styles go as each piece moves.
- rebuild: new AXF app from the closest boilerplate (axf boilerplates), old code kept alongside as reference, rebuilt feature by feature on assets/libraries/plugins.

Deliver: axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild (analysis report: what maps to which asset types, libraries, plugins; then staged codemods like ui-port.mjs does for UI kits), console + MCP drivers, manifest relation none -> built-on when it starts, fixtures/tests. First real targets: xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite) and whatever claude-project parks.

origin.said: ask each time between the two ways.

steps.text: Spec first: `_claude/memory/docs/port-engine.md` — the two modes (bake / rebuild), the analysis report shape (`port-report@1`: stack, UI kit found, screens, chrome pieces → asset types, styles → tokens, libraries/plugins suggested, risk list), the staged codemod plan, and what `axf port` refuses (no manifest, dirty git tree). Read `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` and `claude-project.mjs` first.

CLI entry: `framework/cli/port.mjs` + `axf port <dir> --mode bake|rebuild [--report-only] [--stage N]` in `axf.mjs`; `requireProject` gate; refuses without `--yes` when git is dirty; writes `port-report.json` next to the manifest. `--report-only` works on an empty folder (empty report).

Stack detection: reuse `claude-project.mjs` detection (react/next/android/python…), add UI-kit detection (MUI, Chakra, shadcn, Material3, Compose, Tailwind) by package.json / gradle deps; unit test with fixture folders under `framework/spec/fixtures/port/`.

Analysis, screens + chrome: scan routes/screens (React Router / Next pages / Compose NavHost) and chrome components (app bar, drawer, bottom nav, menus, toolbars, dialogs) → candidate asset list with target type and confidence. Report section `pieces`.

Analysis, styles → tokens: run `portSource` from `ui-port.mjs` in dry mode over the codebase to count colour/size literals and role usages; map to the token list from the theme engine; report `tokens` with unmapped literals. Cap files scanned (size + count) and skip node_modules/build.

Bake, stage 1: `axf init` into the existing project (template by stack) without overwriting app files (`src/axf/` + assets + manifest relation `built-on`), `axf.lock.json`; app still builds (the template guard allows an existing codebase). Checked with a fixture react app.

Bake, stage 2: themes — generate `color-theme` + `style-theme` assets from the detected palette (nearest tokens), apply the literal → `var(--fx-*)` codemod (`ui-port.mjs portSource`) to CSS/TSX/Kotlin files in place with a `.port-backup/`; `--stage 2` only; report lists every file changed.

Bake, stage 3: chrome — generate nav-menu / app-menu / toolbar / dialog assets from the detected pieces and swap the components for the framework ones (`AppShell` / Compose `AppShell`), old components kept under `legacy/` until removed; `--stage 3`.

Rebuild mode: pick the closest boilerplate (`framework/boilerplates/index.json` tags vs detected features), `axf init --boilerplate` into `<dir>-axf` beside the old code, write `PORT-PLAN.md` with screen-by-screen mapping and the old file for each; report `rebuild.plan`.

Drivers: engine-rpc `port` / `port-report`, console `POST /api/port` + `GET /api/port/report?dir=`, MCP `app_port(dir, mode, stage)` (write, needs the console token); manifest `framework.relation` none → built-on when stage 1 runs (`project.mjs` validates).

Console view: Plugins → **Port** (or Wizards view section): pick a folder from allowed roots (project-wizard's `AXF_WIZARD_ROOTS` rule), run the report, show pieces/tokens tables, run stages one at a time with the file list and a diff count; rebuild plan rendered as a checklist.

Pending items hook: `port-<name>` items (parked by claude-project) get a "Run port" button in Pending rows (slot `pending.item`) that opens the console view on that project; `claude-project` writes `x.port.engine: "axf port"` into the manifest.
First real target, xGallery (MossesX/xGallery, React 19 + Express + SQLite): BRETT attaches the repo; run `--report-only`, review the report together, record the mode choice. No codemod yet.
xGallery bake stage 1–2 on a branch in that repo (init + themes), app builds; note unmapped literals; push branch `axf-port` for Brett to look at on the phone.
Tests: `framework/spec/check-port.mjs` over the fixture folders (detection, report shape, stage 1 idempotent, stage 2 backup + dry run, refusals: no manifest, dirty tree, symlinks); CI line.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/app-port-engine.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status + `axf port` in Build/run/test, pending complete; decisions.md note on bake vs rebuild defaults.

Turn xGallery's New project wizard (MossesX/xGallery: server/src/routes/newproject.ts, src/pages/dev/newproject/NewProjectWizard.tsx, kit/new-project.mjs) into an AXF library so every app built on AXF can clone its install into a new project. What the xGallery wizard does today (reuse the design): renamed copy from the kit, GitHub repo, per-project deploy key installed on the VPS + Actions secrets (VPS_SSH_KEY, ADMIN_PASSWORD, HOSTINGER_API_TOKEN), Hostinger DNS for site + dev panel, Claude GitHub app access, push main, wait for the site deploy, push panel, wait, first-session prompt; resumable, no secrets stored.

New for the library: clone WITH current data (database snapshot + media/files, consistent copy, secrets and sessions stripped, owner reset), the copy gets its own project.manifest.json + _claude/ (claude-project), cross-port contract (web + Android) for the clone action exposed through the interop gate (default-deny), a settings tab (plugin manager rules: no own settings screen), console + MCP drivers. steps.text: BRETT decides the two open questions before any code: (1) which data a clone copies by default (database snapshot + media? settings? sessions never), (2) whether users/members come along or the clone starts with the owner only. Write both into this item's notes and `_claude/memory/decisions.md`.

Contract `clone@1`: `framework/core/clone.ts` (TS reference) — `CloneRequest` {name, id, homes (github/vps/local like project-wizard), data: {database, media, settings, users}, stripSecrets: true}, `CloneReport`, pure validators (name/id rules from `claude-project.mjs`), exposure descriptor `clone.run` default-deny REMOTE (INTEROP.md). Fixture `spec/fixtures/clone.json` + `gen-fixtures`.

Kotlin mirror `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.clone` (same validators, `ConformanceTest` replay) + Python `framework/python/axf_libs/clone/contract.py` (used by server parts). Placeholder capability `axf.clone` declared in the kernel.

Library scaffold: `axf new-library clone --template service-provider --ports web,android,python` → `framework/libs/clone` (web `AxfWebLibrary` with a settings group "Clone", no own screen), `framework/android/lib-clone`, `framework/python/axf_libs/clone`; `axf compile-library clone` passes. Catalog `libraries.json` entry.

Data snapshot (server, Python): `axf_libs/clone/snapshot.py` — consistent copy of a SQLite db (`sqlite3 .backup`) and listed media folders into a temp dir, strip secret-looking files (reuse project-wizard's patterns), reset owner per the step-1 decision; unit test on a fixture db.

Homes + kit: reuse `apps/console-web/plugins/project-wizard/wizard.mjs` (`run`, `kit`, `link`) for GitHub/VPS/local homes, manifest, `_claude/`, Claude.ai kit; `clone` calls it with `source: folder` after the snapshot is unpacked into the new folder. One code path, no second copy of the wizard.

Web side: `framework/libs/clone/client.ts` (`CloneClient` over the app's API, token via a credential provider like `libs/mcp`), Settings → Clone group (name, id, data toggles from the decision, homes), progress stream (SSE like project-wizard), done screen with links. Gate: `rt.uac` must hold `clone.run`.

Android side: `lib-clone` `CloneModule` → Settings group + `CloneScreen` route `clone` calling the same API through axf-network; `AxfClone` registers the `axf.clone` provider; written without a compiler, CI `:lib-clone:testDebugUnitTest` with a fake server.

Console + MCP drivers: console plugin-free route `POST /api/clone` (admin only) running the Python engine; MCP `app_clone` (write, confirm required = destructive annotation); the console's own Settings → Plugins lists lib-clone like other libraries.

xGallery hook: xGallery keeps its wizard; add a `clone` endpoint there that imports `axf_libs.clone` (or calls the console API) so its New project wizard's "clone with data" uses the library — only after Brett attaches MossesX/xGallery.

Tests + CI: `framework/spec/check-clone.mts` (fixtures, validators), Python `axf_libs/clone/test.py` (snapshot strips secrets, resets owner, refuses symlinks/outside roots), lifecycle not needed (library). CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/lib-clone.md`, LOG.md, CLAUDE.md Status, `libraries.json`/tracker, pending complete.

builds.title: Plugin conflict alarm + tracked AI patches + installed add-ons list
builds.detail:
Brett, Oct 18 2026 (parked as unsafe: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

1. When a plugin could potentially conflict with another plugin, raise a developer alarm (alerts library, source conflicts) shown as an expandable row grid like the Systems check grid: same kinds of details per row, fix instructions and external links.
2. Each conflict row has 3 badges/actions: (a) uninstall a plugin - choose which one; (b) ignore; (c) use AI to patch the conflict. The patch must NOT alter any plugin source.
3. Patches are tracked and listed in an Installed add-ons list that covers plugins, add-ons, modules, libraries and patches. Installing a patch is tracked and the patch can be removed.
4. Removing a patch uninstalls every conflicting plugin it patched; those plugins must then be reinstalled.

Builds on: alerts library (conflicts source, diagnostics: same asset id / setting key / settings tab from two named modules; plugins:dup ids on the server), plugin-lifecycle@1 (install/uninstall scripts, backups), plugin-manager (Fable, pending), agent manager add-ons (agent-addon@1 install/uninstall tracking), axf.llm@1 for the AI patch.
Open questions for Brett at build time: what counts as a potential conflict beyond the runtime diagnostics (routes, capability services, settings keys, assets, nav ids, CSS prefixes, data dirs?); where patches live (an overlay layer the console applies at load, never the plugin folder); whether removing a patch should back up the plugins first and offer one-tap reinstall.

notes.text: Oct 22 2026: patches-plugins (Opus) adds Patches-owned plugin lists per hosted app and an auto install of missing plugins; check for overlap when this is designed.

origin.said: AI patching and cascading uninstalls need design and review before anyone builds it):

steps.text: Design note, part 1 (no code): `_claude/memory/docs/plugin-conflicts.md` — what counts as a potential conflict beyond runtime diagnostics: routes (`/api/plugins/<f>/`), capability services (two providers of one `axf.x@1`), settings keys, asset ids, nav ids, CSS prefixes (`axp-*`), data dirs, Python module names. For each: how it is detected from `plugin.json` + the bundle + `plugin-inventory@1` facts, severity, false-positive risk.

Design note, part 2: patches. Proposal: a patch is an **overlay** (`.axf-console/patches/<id>/patch.json`, `plugin-patch@1`: target plugins, kind rename-route / remap-setting / alias-asset / disable-contribution, applied by the console at load, never touching a plugin folder); AI only proposes a patch document, a person approves it (change-batch card); removal backs up + offers one-tap reinstall. Risks and what is refused.

BRETT reviews both notes and answers the three open questions (conflict kinds in scope, overlay approach yes/no, backup + reinstall on patch removal). Status stays `unsafe` until he says the design is approved; then `pending`. Record in decisions.md.

Conflict engine (pure): extend `framework/core/engines/plugins.ts` (`plugin-inventory@1`) with `potentialConflicts(records)` for the approved kinds, severity + fix hints; Kotlin `PluginInventoryEngine` + Python `plugin-manager/server/engine.py` mirror it; fixture cases in `spec/fixtures/plugin-inventory.json` → `conflicts` (`check-plugin-inventory.mts`, `test.py`, `PluginInventoryConformanceTest`).

Alerts source `conflicts`: `apps/console-web/server/alerts.py` raises one alert per conflict key (`conflict:<kind>:<a>:<b>`, warn, resolved when it disappears) from the engine output every poll; rule default: bell on. Test in `server/test_alerts.py`.

Conflict grid UI: plugin `apps/console-web/plugins/plugin-conflicts` (from `_template`) with a dialog `plugin-conflicts.grid` built on the Systems check grid component pattern (expandable rows: details, fix instructions, links); opened from the alert's link and from Plugin Manager rows. Read-only this step.

Row actions (a) Uninstall — pick which plugin, confirm by typing its folder, runs `plugin-lifecycle.mjs uninstall --all` through the existing `/api/plugin-lifecycle/<folder>/uninstall`; (b) Ignore — stored per conflict key in the plugin dataDir, hides the row and resolves the alert; both admin-only.

Patch overlay runtime: `server/patches.py` loads `plugin-patch@1` files, validates them against the schema (`framework/schemas/plugin-patch.json`), applies approved kinds at plugin load (route prefix rename, settings key remap, asset alias, contribution disable) in the loader, never writes into plugin folders; `GET /api/plugins/plugin-conflicts/patches`.

(c) AI patch: "Patch with AI" asks Mosses through `axf.llm@1` for a patch document for this conflict (prompt includes the engine facts), validates it, shows it on a change-batch-style approval card; Apply writes the file and reloads plugins; refused when the assistant is off (409 with what is missing).

Installed add-ons list: dialog + Settings → Plugins → Add-ons listing plugins, libraries (`plugin-inventory`), modules, agent add-ons (`agent-addon@1` from `axf.agents@1` when present) and patches, each with installed date, what it touches, Remove. Patches show which plugins they patch.

Patch removal: Remove patch → backup (`.axf-console/plugin-backups/`) → uninstall every plugin it patched (lifecycle) → list them with one-tap Reinstall from the catalog (`plugin-catalog.mjs install`) when the step-3 decision says so. Audit line per action.
Tests: plugin `test.py` (grid data, ignore, patch validation + refusals, removal cascade with fake lifecycle), engine fixtures, lifecycle check, CI lines.
Close: report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/plugin-conflicts.md`, LOG.md, web screenshots, CLAUDE.md Status, rules line about patches never touching plugin folders, pending complete.

builds.detail:
Brett, Oct 20 2026: agents (Build Pilot's pilot-assembler, Mosses and every agent-definition@1 agent) and AI assistant live sessions should run on axHub, not inside each app. Build Pilot, the Dev Console and the phone apps become clients.

- axHub gets an agent + session host: runs turns, owns live-session@1 event logs (sessions survive app restarts and browser closes), per-agent memory, provider keys in axHub's vault, hub permissions for who may use which agent.
- Apps plug in through what the Fable rebuilds left open: the live-session host registry (`axf.live-host@1` / `register_host`, today a typed `axhub` placeholder in the console and Build Pilot), Build Pilot's assembly backend (BP_AGENT=local|console|off → add `axhub`), and the kernel placeholders `axf.agents`, `axhub.agent`.
- axHub never depends on AXF (decision): the host speaks the contracts over its API (AXPP), with an AXF adapter on the AXF side (lib-hub).
- The assembly gate (pilot-assembly@1) stays in Build Pilot: axHub only proposes ops; Build Pilot checks and builds. Manual mode unaffected.
- Needs the axHub repo (MossesX/axHub) attached.

Until then: Build Pilot runs its agent locally (Fable rebuild Oct 20 2026), the console's assistant hosts its own sessions.

steps.text: BRETT attaches MossesX/axHub. Read its session/worker layout, decisions #70–#87 and the AXPP protocol doc; write `_claude/memory/docs/axhub-agent-host.md` design: host API (sessions, turns, events, agents, memory, permissions), where provider keys live (vault, write-only), what the AXF adapter translates. No code.

Protocol contract (AXF side, pure): `framework/core/live-session.ts` gains the wire shape for a remote host (`RemoteHostDescriptor`, event envelope with seq, resume cursor), fixtures in `spec/fixtures/live-session.json` → `remote`; Kotlin `ai.amberx.axf.kernel.live` + Python mirror replay them.

axHub, session store: `sessions` table/collection (id, owner, agent, created, closed, cursor) + append-only event log keyed by seq (file or db per axHub's storage), with replay from a cursor; unit tests.

axHub, turn runner: a worker that runs one turn for a session (provider call through axHub's existing LLM client or a new one using vault keys), streams events into the log, survives the browser going away; one running turn per session; stop/cancel.

axHub, agents: `agent-definition@1` validator ported from `framework/core/agents.ts` (fixture `agents.json` replayed), agent registry per project in `/projects/<name>/_data/agents/`, per-agent memory using the memory engine rules from the contract.

axHub, permissions: who may use which agent / open sessions / write mode, as hub user permissions (`agents.use.<id>`, `sessions.open`, `agents.write`) on the users page, enforced on every host route; admin bypass as elsewhere on the hub.

axHub, host API: `/agents`, `/sessions`, `/sessions/{id}/turns` (POST = run), `/sessions/{id}/events?since=` (SSE + replay), `/sessions/{id}/stop|close`; approvals for destructive tool calls through the hub's approval screen (one-tap link rule). OpenAPI snippet in the design doc.

axHub, provider keys: turns use keys from the vault by name (`llm.<provider>`), never returned; `vault.set` from the console's Keys needed flow already exists — add the names to the systems-check key list on the AXF side later (step 15).

AXF adapter, web: `framework/libs/hub` (lib-hub, first slice exists) gets `AxhubLiveHost implements SessionHost` over the host API with the hub session cookie / token provider; registers through `axf.live-sessions@1.register_host()`; the console's AI assistant picks it when Settings → Assistant → Host = axHub.

AXF adapter, Android: `lib-hub` Kotlin `AxhubLiveHost` over axf-network (SSE reader from `lib-mcp`'s parser), registered in the kernel's live-session host registry; placeholder `axhub.agent` becomes real; written without a compiler, CI unit test with MockWebServer.

Console assistant on the hub host: `ai-assistant` plugin `server/sessions.py` host `axhub` stops being a `PlaceholderHost`: a thin proxy host that forwards to the hub API with the signed-in user's identity; reconnect/replay through the existing `watchReply` fold; `test.py` cases with a fake hub.

Build Pilot: `BP_AGENT=axhub` backend in `server/assembly.py` calling the hub host for the `pilot-assembler` agent; the assembly gate (`pilot-assembly@1`) still checks every op locally; manual mode untouched; `test_server.py` with a fake hub.
Phone apps: the AXHub Android app gets a Sessions tab (list, attach to a live reply, stop) on `lib-hub`'s host client; the Android console's assistant screen (when it exists) uses the same.

Migration: console sessions stored locally can be exported/imported into the hub (`POST /sessions/import` with the event log); one-time "Move my sessions to axHub" button in the assistant settings; no data loss on failure (import is additive).
Systems check: new checks `axhub-agent-host` (host reachable, caller allowed) and the vault key names for providers in the Keys needed list; Auto fix opens the right pages.
Alerts + activity: hub sessions appear in the Activity banner source list (`axf.activity@1`), failed turns raise an alert via the hub → console alerts source `axhub`.
Tests, AXF side: `check-live-session` fixture cases for the remote shape, lib-hub web unit tests (fake SSE), Android unit test, plugin `test.py` additions; CI lines in `android.yml`.
Tests, axHub side: host API tests (permissions, replay from cursor, one turn per session, stop), agent validator fixture replay, vault key never returned.

Deploy: axHub redeploy on Coolify with the worker enabled (env for worker count), console `install-console.sh` passes `AXF_ASSISTANT_HOST=axhub` once the hub answers; BRETT approves the deploy and runs one turn from his phone.
Close: differences report `_claude/memory/docs/rebuilds/axhub-agent-host.md`, LOG.md, decisions.md (#88+ on the hub side), CLAUDE.md Status in both repos, pending complete.

2a. `lib-apptabs` module skeleton: `framework/android/lib-apptabs` (id `ai.amberx.axf.apptabs`, `settings.gradle.kts` entry, `AppTabsModule` registering a settings group "App tabs" with the same keys as the web plugin `app-tabs.tabs|custom|active`); `:lib-apptabs:testDebugUnitTest` job with one test (keys match the web plugin's constants read from a shared JSON resource).

2b. Tab bar composable `AxfAppTabBar` in slot `app.frame.top`: reads the tab list + active id from settings, console tab = the app itself, action `app-tabs.show:<id>` registered; tapping switches the active setting; no content yet.

2c. Settings sync note: the module reads/writes only through `SettingsRegistry` so settings-from-axHub (decision Oct 20) applies once that lands; add the keys to `framework/android/lib-settings`'s shared-key list; unit test round-trip of `app-tabs.custom` JSON.

3a. Built-in tab list: Console (self), Pilot `https://pilot.amberxai.com`, axHub `https://axhub.amberxai.com/apps`, Demo, as a Kotlin list mirroring the web plugin's built-ins; icons from `axf-ui/icons`.

3b. Manifest tabs: project manifests built on/for AXF with `deploy.url`, read from a bundled `catalog/projects.json` (generated by `sync-data.mjs` into the Android console assets), appended to the list; unit test with a fixture catalog.

4a. `AxfWebTab` web view composable, locked down: allowed hosts only (own domains from manifest/settings), refuse other links with a toast (never the outside browser), JavaScript on, file access off, popups off, geolocation off, mixed content blocked; unit test of the allow rule (pure function `hostAllowed`).

4b. `AxfWebTab` state: one WebView per tab, lazily created, retained across recompositions (`remember` + `AndroidView` holder keyed by tab id), `FLAG_SECURE` honoured from the activity; manual check on the emulator that switching tabs keeps scroll position.

5a. Hub session cookies: `CookieManager` scoped to the app, `android:allowBackup` rules + `dataExtractionRules` exclude the WebView data; sign-in happens on the hub's own login page inside the tab (no JS injection, no off-hub navigation).

7b. Loading + errors: pull-to-refresh, a "Loading…" bar, a plain error card (offline, 4xx/5xx, refused frame) with Retry, all from theme tokens; emulator check.
8a. Settings → Plugins → App tabs: pick tabs (switch per built-in), order (up/down), reset; `SettingsGroup`/`SettingSpec` with parent = Plugins.
8b. Custom tabs: add name + https address on an allowed host (validated with `hostAllowed`), remove; stored in `app-tabs.custom` with the web plugin's JSON shape.

builds.title: Patches manages the plugins of the apps it hosts (Opus)
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 22 2026: when Patches loads developer apps in tabs, Patches owns all plugins. New embed@1 take `plugins`: inside such a host an app loads only the plugins Patches has installed and enabled for it (its own on/off switches don't apply), and its plugin hooks (Settings → Plugins, Plugin Manager, plugin switches, plugin menu entries) are greyed out with "Plugins are managed in Patches". builds.title: Asset system (asset@1, 13 core types, open registry)
builds.detail: Every visual is a JSON asset (color theme, style theme, layout, menus, toolbar, nav, context menu, dialog, popup, button, slider, container, UAC policy). Ports read the same files; new types register at runtime.

builds.title: Engines: theme, layout, component styles, UAC, context menu, actions
builds.detail: Compile assets into tokens and behaviour: theme tokens (core + extended), layouts per window class, component styles, role-based access, context menus per target, action bus with interceptors.

builds.title: Kernel (pure Kotlin + TypeScript core)
builds.detail: The framework core every app gets: asset registry, engines, runtime state, actions, module system. Pure Kotlin on Android (no Android imports, KMP-ready); framework/core on the web.

builds.title: Porting spec + conformance fixtures
builds.detail: framework/spec: PORTING.md plus generated fixtures every port must reproduce exactly (theme vars, layouts, component styles, UAC). The Android kernel passes them.

builds.title: Windowing engine: tab groups, floating windows, split, minimize
builds.detail: Window schema (types, toolbar rules), tab groups that undock to floating windows, drag tabs between groups and windows, split vertical / horizontal / four-way / custom grid with even distribution (5 → 3+2), minimize to corner title bars (stacked or lined) or a floating toolbar at the cursor, window settings dialog, tree ↔ grid mode.

builds.title: Output terminal
builds.detail: One append-only log every install, import, hot swap and kit fallback writes to; auto-scrolling pane as a floating window, dock tab or dialog; follows the console API live over SSE.

builds.title: Android framework modules
builds.detail: axf-platform-android, axf-assets, axf-ui (Compose components, kits, element explorer, windows), axf-nav, axf-data, axf-network, axf-devtools, axf-testing. Published as ai.amberx.axf:<module>:0.2.0.

builds.title: Android showcase app (apps/console)
builds.detail: The first Android app: the console views on the Android port (tracker, catalog, libraries, boilerplates, element explorer). Builds a ~20 MB debug APK in CI.

builds.title: Web port: core + React components
builds.detail: framework/core + framework/react + framework/ui/axf.css: the original port, plain React 18 + TypeScript, no router.

builds.title: Web templates: react-ts (Vite) and next-ts (Next.js 15)
builds.detail: axf init creates either a Vite SPA or a Next.js App Router app (static export by default) with the framework baked in.

builds.title: Build engine CLI
builds.detail: axf init / validate / list / new-asset / schemas / templates / new-module / new-demo / modules / boilerplates / dev / serve.

builds.title: Library installer + interactive wizard
builds.detail: Libraries ship a library.json (params, manifest key, install steps); axf install asks for the parameters and writes manifest, gradle, App.kt and typed <Name>Setup.kt. Also runs at pre-build via --libraries / boilerplate libraries.

builds.title: Library browser (installable)
builds.detail: Floating tab-group browser as a library: two panes, multi-select, Compare → floating windows; binds to tab groups named in the app manifest; installed by a wizard.

builds.title: Library templates (build, port, compile new libraries)
builds.detail: Boilerplates for libraries: feature screens, service provider, data feature, device capability, integration, UI kit, background worker, blank — generating Android, web and Python ports, compiling each, and porting a library to another port from its library.json.

builds.title: Web Dev Console (React/TS)
builds.detail: apps/console-web: Home, Tracker, Catalog, Libraries (framework + UI), Boilerplates, Plan, Demos, Modules, Components, Assets, output terminal, floating windows.

builds.title: Console API (Python FastAPI)
builds.detail: Runs the build engine for the console (init, install, import-ui, status edits, boilerplates, plan), streams the terminal over SSE, manages dev servers, serves the console and panel.

builds.title: Planning section
builds.detail: This view: every framework feature with capabilities, ports, dependencies, acceptance, screenshots, previews, warnings, recommendations and history; list and board views; auto warnings for blocked dependencies and port gaps.

builds.title: Server control panel
builds.detail: Dev servers start/stop with logs, CI downloads (APK, Maven, console dist), command catalog, live output and a terminal into the console container.

builds.title: CI: build, test, publish
builds.detail: GitHub Actions: build-engine sweep, kernel tests, every Android module, showcase APK, Maven repo artifact + GitHub Packages, web console + Python API smoke, next-ts build; compile errors posted to an issue.

builds.title: Demo site deployment
builds.detail: CI publishes apps/demo to the site branch; the VPS pulls it every 2 minutes behind Traefik.

builds.title: Web demo site
builds.detail: apps/demo, published by CI to the site branch and served from the VPS.

builds.title: Build manager (build queue)
builds.detail: The plan's epics as an ordered build queue: drag to reorder, reprocess to restore dependency order, rework flags on built steps whose dependencies changed, a suggested model per step and per feature (Fable 5.1 / Opus 5.5 / Sonnet 5.5), and two-way status sync with the feature tracker on every console start.

builds.title: MCP server (Model Context Protocol)
builds.detail: The console API as MCP tools for Claude: plan search/edit, build queue (next, reorder, reprocess, complete), catalog status, libraries, templates, app init/validate, terminal. Remote at console.amberxai.com/mcp (streamable HTTP, Bearer AXF_TOKEN) or local over stdio via .mcp.json.

builds.title: Module system: modules, extension points, services, placeholders
builds.detail: Modules register screens, actions, settings, dialogs, services and UI kits through extension points, start in dependency order and can define their own extension points. Placeholders answer NotImplemented until a real module arrives.

steps.text: Web extension registry: `framework/core/extensions.ts` = Kotlin `module/Extensions.kt` (`ExtensionPoint`, `Contribution`, `ExtensionRegistry` with declare/contribute/list/listeners, `ExtensionPoints` with the same ids `axf.actions` … `axf.event-descriptors`); exported from `core/index.ts`; `rt.extensions` on `AxfRuntime`.

Web placeholders: `NotImplemented` answers for undeclared capabilities (`rt.capability(id)` → placeholder record with reason), same shape as the kernel's `placeholder(id)`; `framework/react/library.ts` `installLibraries` routes `provides` into the registry so a library can declare its own points.

Fixture: `spec/fixtures/extensions.json` (declare order, contribution order by `order` then insertion, single vs multiple points, placeholder answers) generated from the TS reference; Kotlin `ConformanceTest` replays it (written without a compiler; check the CI issue).

Topological start order on web: `orderLibraries` (already in `library.ts`) becomes the shared `startOrder(modules)` used by both ports' rules (cycle = error listing members), fixture cases added; `installLibraries` reports `missing` + `cycles`.

Python port: `framework/python/axf/extensions.py` (`ExtensionRegistry`, standard points, placeholders) replacing the `MemoryKernel` stand-in in `library.py`; `axf compile-library` smoke test uses it; fixture replay test `framework/python/axf/test_extensions.py`.
Services: typed service registry on web (`rt.services.register/get` with `service:<cap>` names as `plugin-inventory@1` uses) + Python; inventory engine reads providers from it; one fixture case.

Docs + status: `framework/spec/PORTING.md` section "Extension points on every port", plan ports web/python → built, `status.json` features for the epic's capabilities, `tracker.mjs`, `build_step complete`.

Template + console: `react-ts`/`next-ts` templates and the console register one custom extension point each (proves "add modules without rebuilding the kernel"); console tsc + vite build; CI template sweep passes.

builds.title: Console deployment (install-console.sh)
builds.detail: One command on the VPS builds the console + API + panel container behind Coolify Traefik with HTTPS at console.amberxai.com, prints AXF_TOKEN and auto-updates every 5 minutes.

builds.title: State, data cache, events, flags, config, migrations
builds.detail: AxfStore (reducer/middleware/undo), QueryClient (stale-while-revalidate), EventBus, layered FeatureFlags and Config, migrations ledger + semver.

steps.text: Web `AxfStore` in `framework/core/state/store.ts` mirroring Kotlin `state/Store.kt` (reducer, middleware chain, undo/redo, `StatePersistence` over the settings store); unit cases in a new fixture `spec/fixtures/state.json` (reduce, middleware order, undo).

Web `QueryClient` in `core/state/query.ts` = Kotlin `data/QueryEngine.kt` (stale-while-revalidate, `Freshness`, `QueryOptions`, dedupe in-flight, persistence hook); fixture section `query` with fake timers encoded as explicit clock values.
Web `EventBus` (`core/state/events.ts` = `event/EventBus.kt`: topics, replay buffer, typed kernel events) wired to the runtime's existing `on()`; fixture section `events` (replay count, ordering).

Web `FeatureFlags` + `Config` (`core/state/flags.ts`, `config.ts` = `flags/FeatureFlags.kt`, `config/Config.kt`: layers DEFAULT/MANIFEST/REMOTE/ROLE/USER/KILL_SWITCH and DEFAULTS/MANIFEST/REMOTE/USER/OVERRIDE, precedence); manifest `flags`/`config` read at `createAxf`; fixture sections.

Web migrations ledger + semver (`core/state/migrations.ts` = `migrate/Migrations.kt`: `Migration`, `MigrationRunner`, ledger in settings, `Semver` compare, `Deprecations`); the console's one-time saved-defaults migration moves onto it; fixture section `migrations`.

Kotlin conformance: `StateConformanceTest` replaying `state.json` against the existing kernel classes (adjust kernel behaviour only where the fixture exposes a real divergence; note each in the commit); written without a compiler.
React hooks: `useStore`, `useQuery`, `useFlag`, `useConfig` in `framework/react/state.ts`; the console's Plan view uses `useQuery` for `plan.json` as the first consumer; tsc + vite build.
Docs + status: PORTING.md section, plan web port → built (python stays planned), status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

builds.title: UI-kit switching + fallback
builds.detail: Every component is an abstract kind; the active ui-kit asset picks which library renders it. Kinds a kit lacks fall back to the default AmberX kit and are noted on the output terminal.

steps.text: Web kit contract: `framework/core/uikit.ts` = Kotlin `contract/UiKit.kt` (`ComponentKind` list from `ui-port.mjs` `COMPONENT_KINDS`, `UiKitSpec`, `UiKitResolver` with fallback to the default AmberX kit + terminal note per missing kind); fixture `spec/fixtures/uikit.json` (resolve, fallback, note text).

React kit registry: `framework/react/kits/index.ts` with the built-in `amberx` kit (today's components mapped by kind) and `registerKit(spec, impl)`; `AppShell`/`Controls` resolve each kind through the resolver instead of importing components directly.

ui-kit asset wiring: the active `ui-kit` asset (already an asset type on Android) picks the kit on web too; Settings → Appearance → UI kit drop-down (both ports share the setting key); rolls exclude it (`rollDefaults.never`).

Second kit (proof): `framework/libs/kit-mui` skeleton via `axf new-library kit-mui --template ui-kit --ports web` with 6 kinds (BUTTON, TEXT_FIELD, SWITCH, CARD, DIALOG, TOAST) on MUI reading only `--fx-*` tokens (THEMING.md); missing kinds fall back and are listed in the Output terminal.
Kotlin parity check: `UiKitConformanceTest` replaying `uikit.json` against `UiKitResolver`; `check-theme.mjs` covers `libs/kit-*`.
Python placeholder: `framework/python/axf/uikit.py` resolver replaying the fixture (Qt Widgets kit stays planned, a placeholder capability `axf.uikit.qt`).
Docs + status: PORTING.md "UI kits", plan web → built, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

builds.title: Libraries: settings, logging, admin, accounts, profile, billing
builds.detail: The six libraries the console and apps build on. Settings and logging are complete; accounts and billing run on mock providers.

steps.text: Scope note first: `_claude/memory/docs/libs-core.md` — for each of admin, accounts, profile, billing: what the Android placeholder has (`lib-admin`, `lib-accounts`, `lib-profile`, `lib-billing` screens + modules), what "real" means per port (accounts = axHub provider from `x.session`; billing = provider interface only, Play Billing as a separate library per the plan's recommendation), the web library ids (`ai.amberx.axf.<name>`).

Web lib-logging: `framework/libs/logging` (`AxfWebLibrary`: log sinks via `ExtensionPoints.LOG_SINKS`, levels, the Output terminal as default sink, Settings → General → Logging group) matching `lib-logging` on Android; `axf init` web templates install it beside settings.

Web lib-accounts: `framework/libs/accounts` (Account view = today's `react/studio/AccountView.tsx` moved into the library, sign-in/out through `rt.session` providers, Settings → Account group); the console installs it.

Android lib-accounts real: `AccountsModule` consumes `AUTH_PROVIDERS` (from `x.session` step 4), `AccountScreen` shows the provider's principal, sign-in/out, errors; mock provider moved to `lib-accounts-mock`; `lib-accounts` unit test with a fake provider.

Profile: `lib-profile` Android (`ProfileScreen` edits display name/avatar stored per principal in KV, exported through a `ProfileProvider` interface) + web `framework/libs/profile` (same provider interface, avatar widget uses `avatar` widget kind); contract in `core/profile.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Profile.kt`.

Admin: `lib-admin` Android + web `framework/libs/admin`: an admin-only view (UAC `admin.*`) listing modules/libraries (plugin-inventory), audit log, flags toggles (`x.state` flags), feature kill switches; hidden entirely without the role.

Billing: provider contract `core/billing.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Billing.kt` (products, entitlements, purchase flow result, restore), `BILLING_PROVIDERS` typed; `lib-billing` Android with a `NoBilling` provider (entitlements empty) and `SubscriptionScreen` driven by the provider; web `framework/libs/billing` same; Play Billing library parked as a plan feature (`x.lib.billing.play`).
Fixtures + Kotlin tests: `spec/fixtures/libs-core.json` (profile validation, billing entitlement rules, admin role gate) replayed on both ports; written without a compiler.
Templates: `axf init` installs logging + accounts + profile on web/Android by default (settings already is), build options unchanged; CI template sweep + `axf validate` on the generated apps.

Catalog + status: `libraries.json` entries for the six on web/android/python(planned), status.json features `a.admin`, `u.accounts`, `p.profile`, `b.subs` → built (billing = contract + NoBilling), tracker, `build_step complete`.
Console: Settings → Account & security uses lib-accounts/profile; Standards → nothing changes; console tsc + vite build; theme-swap script passes on the new views.
Docs: PORTING.md "Core libraries", CLAUDE.md Status bullet, `_claude/memory/docs/libs-core.md` finished with what stayed placeholder (Play Billing).

builds.title: Import third-party UI libraries → AmberX kits
builds.detail: axf import-ui clones (git/local) or records (maven/npm) a library, rewrites literals and Material/MUI roles to AXF tokens, saves kit-<id> + its ui-kit asset and applies it to the open project.

steps.text: Real-library trial: run `axf import-ui --name Cupertino --kit cupertino --source git --path <compose-cupertino repo>` into a scratch android-compose app (`/tmp`), read `tokens.map.json`, list what the codemod missed (patterns + counts) in `_claude/memory/docs/uiport-trial.md`.

Codemod fixes from the trial: extend `ROLE_MAP`/`guessToken` in `framework/cli/ui-port.mjs` for the missed Compose patterns (e.g. `MaterialTheme.colorScheme.x`, `Modifier.padding(Nn.dp)` → space tokens), unit cases in `framework/spec/check-uiport.mjs` (new; fixture snippets in `spec/fixtures/uiport/`).

Kit overrides: generated `kit-<id>` module gets per-kind override files from the library's components (mapping table in `tokens.map.json` → `components.map.json`), default components kept where unmapped; the ui-kit asset lists `covers`.
Web side: `import-ui` for npm libraries (MUI first) generating `framework/libs/kit-<id>` from the `ui-kit` library template with the same maps; `check-theme.mjs` passes on the output.
CI + status: `check-uiport.mjs` in `android.yml` (node job) + the existing fake-lib import sweep; plan warnings cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

builds.title: Live reload (axf dev) + device hot reload
builds.detail: axf dev watches assets and long-polls changes to devices; the Android HotReloader re-registers changed assets live.

steps.text: Web hot reload: `framework/react` `useDevServer(url)` long-polls `/events` from `dev-server.mjs` and re-registers changed assets (`registry.register` + `rt.refreshFromSaved`); `axf dev` prints the URL; demo app opts in with `?axfDev=`.

Android end to end on the emulator (CI): `rebuild-shots.yml`-style job step that starts `axf dev --framework` on the runner, points the emulator at `10.0.2.2:7070` (setting `axf.devServer`, flag `axf.hotReload`), edits a theme file, screenshots before/after and asserts the pixel diff > 0.

Robustness: dev server validates every changed file before announcing it (invalid → `/events` carries `error` and the device shows a terminal line), ignores editor temp files, handles rename/delete; `check-dev-server.mjs` test with a temp folder.
Docs + status: README section "Live reload on a phone" (PC IP, same Wi-Fi), plan warning cleared, status.json + tracker, `build_step complete`.

builds.title: Session, principal, audit log
builds.detail: Session/Principal/SessionProvider contracts and an AuditLog service; accounts library uses a mock auth provider.

steps.text: Web contract: `framework/core/session.ts` = Kotlin `contract/Session.kt` (`Principal`, `Session`, `SessionState`, `SessionProvider`, `AnonymousSession`, `AuditEntry`, `AuditLog`, `MemoryAuditLog`); `rt.session` replaces the ad-hoc principal in `runtime.ts` (`bindPrincipal` keeps working, built on it); fixture `spec/fixtures/session.json` (state transitions, audit cap).

Theme engine: `axf/engines/theme.py` (color + style compile, spacing scale, opacity tokens) replaying `theme.json` + `spacing.json`.
Layout engine: `axf/engines/layout.py` (`compile_slots`, `region_accepts`, hidden regions) replaying `layout.json`, `layout-slots.json`, `hide.json`.
Components engine: `axf/engines/components.py` (component styles, toolbar/nav/app-menu style inputs, container collapsible, toolbar collapsible) replaying `components.json`.
UAC + actions: `axf/engines/uac.py`, `actions.py` replaying `uac.json`, `actions.json`, `menu-filter.json`.
Roll + search engines: `axf/engines/roll.py`, `search.py` replaying `roll.json`, `search.json`.
Banner + widgets engines: `axf/engines/banner.py`, `widgets.py` (host registry, kinds rules) replaying `banner.json`, `widgets.json`.
Runtime: `axf/runtime.py` (registry, swap, settings store, hidden slots, attachments, bound principal, session from `x.session`) with the same action ids; smoke test registering the starter assets.
Project gate: `axf/project.py` validator replaying `project-manifest.json` (same rules file), used by the pyqt6 template's guard.

PyQt6 shell, part 1: `axf/qt/shell.py` — window with banner, menubar (app-menu), toolbar, nav (side list), content region from the compiled layout; theme tokens → Qt stylesheet via a token→QSS compiler.
PyQt6 shell, part 2: dialogs/popups, context menu, settings window driven by `SettingsGroup`s (lib-settings python), search bar widget, clock widget; hot-swap re-applies QSS live.

builds.title: Fix: switches and tab buttons dead inside interface tabs
builds.detail: Brett Oct 27 2026: Appearance switches in console settings and the layout (interface) buttons at the top do nothing. builds.title: Share Search: programmable grid toolbar plugin (search/filter bar + 5 buttons + advanced search), attach to grids
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): make a plugin with a toolbar of programmable actions for filtering, sorting and searching grids. Toolbar name: Share Search. HELD: Brett said 'send to orchestrator and hold off on build' — don't start until he says.

Asked, in full:
- Toolbar config lives in one of several settings groups inside the plugin's settings interface (Settings → Plugins → Share Search). Set what each toolbar item looks like, how it behaves and what it does.
- At app launch, if the plugin isn't attached to any data (grid), prompt with a dialog to attach it: lists every grid in a grid with expanding rows. Can attach to several; each attachment has its own saved settings, look, style and actions.
- Search bar can be a Filter or a Search (switch in its settings); updates the list in real time on every keystroke.
- Toolbar settings are in a tab list inside the plugin settings: one tab per attachment.
- Quick access: right-click on the toolbar → context menu item opens that toolbar's settings in a dialog.
- The search bar's settings sit in the toolbar settings' Appearance section: a collapsible container with an 'Inherit from shell' switch above it, collapsed by default. When inherit is off the container becomes expandable and shows every individual style token and setting as in the main app's settings.
- Along with the search bar: 5 toolbar buttons configured to manage the grid's view and actions, plus a button that opens an Advanced search & filter dialog.
- Install the plugin on the Console NOT attached to anything, to test the attach prompt dialog.

Design notes (proposed, Brett to confirm at build start): default 5 buttons = Sort (column + direction menu), Quick filter (per-column), Columns (show/hide), Expand/collapse all, Density (compact toggle) + Advanced search button. Toolbar config stored as a toolbar asset per attachment so it's hot-swappable. Plugin rules apply: framework controls only (inherits app style), plugin-lifecycle@1 install/uninstall, builtWith, settings sub-tab of Plugins, snaps never overlaps (Oct 28 rule), context-menu link via rt.addContextItems. Clash check: pending-grid-view (Pending builds grid toolbar) and opus/orchestrator-grid use the same lib-datagrid — build after/with them; Share Search can later attach to those grids. Android twin of the grid-attach seam is a deferred gap (Android hold).

builds.title: Run unless blocked: 2-min countdown → urgent alarm (red banner + loud AmberX ring) → 1-min grace → runs; Block anytime; zero session tokens
builds.detail:
Brett Oct 28 2026 (claude.ai): 'Can you send notification that a command is about to be ran and I can intercept it from the banner and block it before axhub tries sending it.' HELD: queued, not started. Picks (cards): profile Refactor, held; countdown 2 minutes.

Design: a third tool policy next to allow / confirm, e.g. 'veto' (run unless blocked). A session's call returns a job id at once; axHub holds the call for the countdown (default 2 min, per-tool override possible later) and immediately pushes through the AmberX app (rule: all axHub pushes come from AmberX) and shows it in the console's banner (approvals banner or its own) with the reason title, the exact call, a live countdown, Block and Run now. No action = runs at zero. Block = cancelled, never runs, the session sees 'blocked' when it next looks at the job. Sessions never poll during the countdown: they carry on and read the job result once at the end only if they need it, which saves the re-read cost of approval checks. Approvals (confirm) stay for risky calls: deletes and free-form root shell. Brett picks which tools move to veto (proposal: merge-pr, redeploys, container restarts). Every veto call is logged with its outcome (ran / blocked / ran early) in the approvals history (approval-costs build). Related: approval-costs (history, wait call, resume), axhub-github-write.

steps.text: card@1 asset type in framework/schemas/asset-types.json (+ axf schemas): id, owner (plugin id or "console"), title, icon, kind (stat | list | meter | chart | feed | status | actions | custom), size (s | m | l | wide | tall), data {service (plugin_services capability), path, refreshSec, live:boolean}, slots (headline, value, sub, rows, sparkline, actions), emptyState, actions (ids run through the action engine), level (Simple/Basic/Developer/Administrator), minRole (UAC), defaultVisible, order, category. builds.title: PR browser + Batch Manager
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Grid of push batches with live badges, Merge/Hold on rows, expandable PR sub-grid, failing check + Fix. Dense: small type, small badges, no clutter. Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

Left click opens review, right click menu. PR BROWSER (Brett, Oct 31): a tab listing every open PR across AmberX-AXF, axHub and Build-Pilot. One dense line per PR with everything: number, title, branch, built by (agent/session), live checks badge, behind main, mergeable/conflict, in which batch, age, cost. Expand a row: every check with its error lines, files changed, commits, description, linked build/plan, and actions: Fix, Merge (via batch), Add to batch, Close. Sort/search/filter like every grid; live updates. ROW LEAD (Brett): every row starts with the PR number + a plain-English line of what it does (e.g. '#187 Audio Extract: pulls audio out of screen recordings, no mic'), written from the actual diff not just the title; badges follow on the same line. SCREENSHOTS (Brett): every PR gets BEFORE (main) and AFTER (PR branch) screenshots of the screens it touches, captured automatically by CI/headless browser (web) and emulator (Android); small before/after thumbnails on the row, side-by-side or slider compare in the expanded view, stored with the PR. SCREENSHOT CORRECTION (Brett): do NOT build a new capture system - REUSE the existing pre-build and post-build screenshots the framework already takes (find them first). BEFORE = the existing pre-build screenshot. AFTER: if the PR/build is not done yet, show a PREDICTED screenshot (rendered mockup of the expected result from the build spec + diff so far, clearly badged 'Predicted'); as soon as the build finishes, the real post-build screenshot replaces it automatically (badge 'Real'), live, no refresh. FEATURE SHOTS (Brett): the existing pre/post-build screenshots are NOT enough - they must show the ACTUAL FEATURE the PR built. Per PR, build a feature map from the diff (changed plugins, components, routes, menus, dialogs -> the screens and states that show them). Drive the existing capture tooling to navigate to each one, open it (expand the row, open the dialog/menu, switch the tab, put it in the right state with demo data), and shoot it: BEFORE on main, AFTER on the PR branch. Each shot cropped to the feature plus a full-screen version, web + Android. Brand-new UI has no before: show a 'New' card. Every feature shot shows Predicted (mockup from spec + diff) until the build is done, then the real shot replaces it live. Captions say which feature each shot is. Missed features (no shot) flagged on the row.

builds.title: Framework grid: built-in sort, search, filter + Date and time column
builds.detail: Brett, Oct 30 2026 (voice): Every grid that lists builds, tasks, asks or anything else is sortable, searchable and filterable, taking little screen. Basic filter attached by default. Tap header sorts, tap again reverses, long-press adds a second sort. One thin row: small search box + filter icon; on phones just a search icon. Filters hidden until used, then small clearable chips. Custom tables move onto the framework grid. Android parity. Per grid: right-click a grid or its header -> Filter -> off/on for this grid; 'All grids...' lists every grid in the app with the right-clicked one scrolled into view and highlighted, a switch per grid; a default switch decides whether new grids get the filter (on). Defaults are decided per grid by the build: on for data grids with many rows or columns (builds, asks, changes, plugins, PRs), off for small lists (settings, keys, short pickers); record the choice and reason per grid. On grids where it is off, hovering the header for a moment shows a tooltip 'Add the filter to this grid?' with Enable (long-press on phones). Framework grid (part of the app, not the filter plugin): every grid that has no date/time column gets an automatic 'Date and time' column (row created / last changed), hidden by default; grids that already show a date/time get nothing. Right-click the header -> Show/Hide 'Date and time'. Web + Android. UPDATE (Brett): build BOTH into the framework grid. Sort/search/filter live in the framework (not the Basic filter plugin); smart per-grid defaults, right-click on/off, All grids list and hover offer all framework features. Date and time column is ensured at first render: if a grid renders without one, the framework adds the hidden column then. New grids get everything automatically. CI check flags any table not built on the framework grid.
